meta.what: The CONVERSION POD library. A pod is a self-contained 3-tweet selling unit — POINT -> BRIDGE -> PLUG — that carries its own setup and can be dropped into any topically-compatible thread. Written once, optimized once, reused. See pods.mjs for the rules and the validator.
meta.operator: 2026-08-21 — 'a combination of a point, the bridge, and the CTA. 3 elements, and we would just reuse them in different threads.'
meta.lockedVsFree: LOCKED (never varies within a pod): the criterion, the substance, the product, the opener move, the beat count, the #ad + link block. FREE (must genuinely differ per account): every other word. The free half is REWRITTEN, not nudged — a near-duplicate detector compares word shingles, so a copy with a few synonyms swapped still scores as a duplicate. podIssues() enforces a Dice ceiling of 0.55 between any two variants, set under fill-queue's 0.72 duplicate flag so the library can never emit text our own scheduler would refuse.
meta.oneVariantPerAccount: RETIRED 2026-08-26 (operator): one reviewed template per product, not one rendering per account. We recreate existing threads, so a repeated CTA is not a new duplicate-content risk. Revisit when threads are written from scratch.
meta.status: experimental -> proven -> retired, promoted on measured revenue exactly like molds.json. A new pod starts experimental.
meta.provenance: A pod is REVERSE-ENGINEERED from a thread that actually converted, not invented. The `measured` block on each pod records the source draft and the Levanta numbers it earned, so 'is this pod any good' is answered from data rather than taste. Fleet baseline CVR at extraction time (2026-08-21, 300 subids, 20,462 clicks): 3.55%.
meta.basis: measured.basis says WHERE the numbers come from. 'thread' = reverse-engineered from one draft, so the copy below is that thread's actual copy and sourceDraft names it. 'aggregate' = the product's pooled rate across many threads and accounts, which is a more reliable RATE but means the copy here is newly written to the winning criterion rather than lifted. An aggregate pod is a stronger bet on the PRODUCT and a weaker one on the COPY; a thread pod is the reverse.
meta.shared_variants: account "*" = shared rotation pool (operator 2026-08-23: per-account plug voice is unnecessary friction). Any account renders a pool variant; an account-specific variant always overrides; the pick is deterministic per (pod, account). WRITING RULE for pool variants: first-person but NO account-specific scenes, names, cities, sports or body parts tied to one persona — "six weeks in, mornings stopped starting flat" travels, "my knees on leg day" does not. Each pod wants a pool of 2-3 so same-day accounts do not share a wording; divergence ceiling applies inside the pool like anywhere else.
meta.two_tweet_bridge_rule: A 2-tweet pod's BRIDGE is its only setup, so it must OPEN on the mechanism — what the substance does, or why the entry line's symptom happens — before any form/dose criterion (operator 2026-08-23: 'How does it go from stairs to CoQ10??? It is missing a bridge in between'). A 3-tweet pod's POINT does this job; a bridge that jumps straight to ubiquinone-vs-ubiquinol reads as a non sequitur under a symptom entry line.
meta.shape: Each pod carries FIVE first tweets, one per frame (framePoints), because the host thread decides what an item IS: a substance, a symptom, an action, a cause, or an answer. The bridge and the plug are shared across all five. T2 opens "But" and names the wrong-form PHYSICAL penalty before handing over the rule; T3 opens by acting on that rule, makes the FORM the cause, and lands three plain benefits. `light` is the no-bridge plug (point -> plug) and needs its own opener, because the heavy opener acts on a rule a light placement never gave the reader.
meta.source: The 19 rewritten pods (all live; NO1 came back on main with a citrulline listing that mints) were written and approved by the operator in the burner account's "cta" drafts. pods.json and those drafts are kept identical — `node sync-cta-drafts.mjs --check` fails CI if they drift.
meta.lineBreaksAreOurs: Wording is the operator's. LINE BREAKS are the engine's, set by checks.mjs: unstackParagraphs on every first tweet and plug beat, airyParagraphs on the bridge, and airyParagraphs again on the first tweet when renderPod is called with light:true (in a light placement that tweet IS the tweet before the plug, so it inherits bridgeWallIssue's stricter rule). A pod's first tweet is item N inside a host thread, never tweet 1, so stackedSentenceIssue's i===0 exemption never covers it. 47 fields were re-spaced on load and not one word changed.
meta.copyEdits: 2026-08-30, SIX words inserted into approved copy, and nothing else. plugSubstanceMismatch reads the plug tweet ALONE against the linked bottle's title, and routes a plug that never names it into the rewrite branch — so the reviewed copy would have been overwritten by the model in production. Inserted: O1 "a cheap omega-3 softgel", B1 "the cheap cyano B12", CO1 "hydrolyzed collagen peptides", PB1 "I bought my probiotic on", TH1 light "I only buy magnesium threonate", W1 "Look at whey protein per 100g". Every other word is as approved.

systems.framed: The 2026-08-30 rewrite. ONE reviewed template per product, FIVE first tweets (one per frame), plus a dedicated light plug. Variety lives between FRAMES. No conversion data yet.
systems.classic: What shipped before it, restored verbatim 2026-08-30. One body per pod reused across all five frames, and a separate wording per ACCOUNT — 63 variants across 10 accounts. Every measured number in this file was earned by this copy.
systems.how: Set POD_SYSTEM=classic to run the old library; anything else runs framed. variantFor filters on the tag, so product facts (asin, criterion, forms, measured) stay single-sourced and cannot drift between the two.

meta.skeleton: SKELETON SYSTEM (operator 2026-09-13; docs/cta-spec.md §0b). A variant tagged system:"skeleton" carries SLOTS, not finished copy: plug.criterion[] (the form criterion as a question answered in the same breath), plug.protocol[], plug.months[] (the since-month every measured winner shares), plug.outcome[] (LITERAL — what you can now do or stopped doing), plug.cta[] (an "I <verb>" possessive), light.opener[], light.cta[]. renderPod assembles the plug; the point, bridge and entry lines are inherited from the pod's backline variant. criterion[0] and cta[0] are the measured best and ship by default (conversion first); protocol, month and outcome rotate per account. The finished-copy systems below are untouched and remain the A/B control: POD_SYSTEM=backline restores them fleet-wide.
